annotations.text:
A · INSTRUMENT — three equal columns, balanced.
Axis: every metric weighted the same.
Good: predictable, you learn where things live.
Tradeoff: nothing draws your eye when something is wrong. Right now RAM is at 86.7% with swap nearly full, and this layout whispers it.

B · TELEMETRY — trend leads, instant value follows.
Axis: time over precision.
All three traces are real 74-second captures at 1 Hz. Note how differently they behave: CPU ramps and decays, memory drifts inside a 1.6 GB band, disk is pure spikes.
Tradeoff: the process lists get squeezed to fit the charts.

C · SIGNAL — the layout reorders itself by severity.
Axis: attention, not symmetry.
Memory is the problem right now, so it takes the wide panel and the 112px numerals; CPU and storage drop to nominal rails.
Tradeoff: the layout moves as conditions change, so muscle memory never forms. Also needs a threshold policy you have to define.

D · MATRIX — maximum density, everything is a grid.
Axis: information per pixel.
128 memory cells at one GiB each; 107 real thermal sensors (23 CPU, 84 GPU) shaded across their observed range, not an absolute scale, so genuine 1-3°C spread stays visible.
Tradeoff: reads as texture at a glance, not as numbers. Best if you look closely.

SIZING — the panel is 1280x480 at backing scale 1.0 over 7 inches, so about 195 PPI with no HiDPI. Type renders at roughly 56% of its usual physical size, which is why body text sits at 11-12px here and hero numerals run 52-112px. Compare A and D: D trades type size for density and is the one to check first on the real screen.

DATA — every number is measured from this machine. Boards A and C use a loaded capture (Safari at 88.8%); B and D use a later idle capture, which is why their headline figures differ. That is deliberate: it shows each layout under two machine states.
